approach: Root cause: the pre-verification mirror registry (crates/athena-core/src/mirrors.rs, run at the producer step by mirror_drift_in in run/producer.rs through check_all) never compared a finished prompt file or new decision-log entry with the structure it must keep. Job 20261015-095214-y8kr (two bullets joined in reader.md) and job 20261025-034452-wqp8 (D122 inserted inside D121) were found only at the final verdict. Fix it in the registry, so the producer loop and the candidate/test gate run it with no new call site. Add two Rule variants and two REGISTRY entries. (1) `PromptStructure`, mirror glob `crates/*/prompts/*.md`, source GitHead, via new `Mirror::files` and `Mirror::covers`. Per prompt file it compares base and new text and finds: (a) a base list item head (marker `- `, `* ` or `<digits>. `, with its leading words) that now sits mid-line in a new line, which is a joined item; (b) a new line, absent from the base, that holds a second list marker glued after text with or without a space (`a.- b: ...`, `it.2. Text ...`). (2) `DecisionEntries`, mirror docs/decisions.md, source GitHead. When the base is a byte prefix of the new text it judges only entries and headings starting at or after the end of the base: heading shape, no repeated or descending id, id one greater than the previous, and a Provenance bullet inside the entry's own span. The parse and these checks live in ONE function pair in mirrors.rs (`parse_decision_entries`, `decision_log_problems`) that the athena-cli log guard `check_log` now calls too, so there is a single definition of a well-formed log (answers finding 7). `append_only_problem` also names the entry that holds the first changed base line ('in D121') or, when the change starts exactly at a heading, 'before D122'. The rules judge structure, not intent: the job carries no machine-readable intended edit, so what is checked is that list items stay one per line and entries stay whole, which is exactly what the two jobs broke. Prompt files are not edited.

A registry entry needs no new call site and covers the whole class of prompt and decision-log files.

decisions.choice: Treat every list marker as an item start in both prompt rules: `- `, `* ` and `<digits>. `. Heads are collected from all three. Head of a `-`/`*` item = marker plus text up to and including the first `:` within 40 chars; otherwise (and for numbered items) the first 24 chars of the line when it has at least 8. Rule (b) matches a glued marker with an optional space for `-` and `*` and only without a space for numbered items.
decisions.reason: The request's cause is 'each instruction still its own bullet'. Grep by the critic found 15 numbered lines in crates/athena-context/prompts/contract.md and crates/athena-cap-study/prompts/verifier.md; joining contract rules 1 and 2 must be caught. Rule (b) must catch the exact y8kr no-space shape (`suffice.- deliverables:`) when both items are new.

rejected.why: Leaves numbered instruction lists unchecked, the same class.

rejected.option: Require a space before a glued dash marker

decisions.choice: Guard rule (b) against prose: a glued `-` needs an alphanumeric or sentence-end char (`. ! ? ; : ) ] " '`) right before it; a space-separated `-` or `*` needs a sentence-end char before the space; a `*` glued without space needs a sentence-end char; a numbered marker needs a sentence-end char directly before it that is not itself preceded by a digit (so `1.2. Then` and `*emphasis* note:` are not flagged); only lines absent from the base are judged.
decisions.reason: Keeps false positives low (criterion 3) while catching both joined shapes; a rewording of one item changes no other line's markers.

rejected.why: Em-dash style prose would be sent back.

decisions.choice: Judge only what the diff adds: prompt rule (a) and (b) look at new lines not in the base; the log rule looks at entries and headings starting at or after the end of the base, and only when the base is an exact byte prefix of the new text.
decisions.reason: The job holds no machine-readable intended edit, so intent cannot be compared; the broken structures are checkable. demonstrations.method: Unit test intended_edits_and_untouched_legacy_text_produce_no_findings runs check_entry for both new entries: (a) a prompt where only one item's wording changes (words after its `- word:` head, and a reworded head), other items and line count unchanged; (b) a base prompt with a mid-line ` - note:` phrase on an unchanged line; (c) prose `see version 1.2. Then stop` and `*emphasis* note: x` in a new line; (d) a change to crates/demo/src/notes.md, which the glob does not cover; (e) a decisions.md whose base holds a legacy entry with no Provenance and an unshaped heading `## D05 (x) · t`, with a well-formed next entry appended; (f) text appended to the last base entry's body. Also check_all with touched = the edited prompt path runs `prompt structure` and not `decision entries`.
demonstrations.observes: check_entry returns an empty Vec for every case; check_all with the prompt path touched returns no Drift and does not call the log rule.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the prompt rule judged every line or the log rule every entry, the legacy cases (b) and (e) fail; if head matching were loose, case (a) fails; if the glued-marker guard were missing, case (c) fails.

demonstrations.observes: Broken edit: producer run count 2; the second producer prompt holds `## Sent back`, the mirror sentence, the file path, the bullet text or entry id and the fix phrase; UI line `producer   sent back: files kept by hand disagree`.
